name: Paradyes
tagline: Semi-permanent hair colour brand from Ahmedabad
excerpt: Ahmedabad hair colour brand Paradyes set off a bidding war on Shark Tank India Season 2 and chose Aman Gupta and Vineeta Singh.
content:
Paradyes sells semi-permanent hair colours in bright shades, aimed at young buyers who want to experiment without long-term damage. It is based in Ahmedabad and was founded by Yushika Jolly and Siddharth Raghuvanshi.

In Shark Tank India Season 2, Episode 9, the founders offered 1% for ₹65 lakh. Business Today reported sales of ₹3.5 crore for FY22. Every shark on the panel made an offer, from 4% to 5% for the same amount. The founders insisted on working with Aman Gupta and Vineeta Singh, and closed at ₹65 lakh for 2%, a ₹32.5 crore valuation. Anupam Mittal and Peyush Bansal withdrew, and the negotiation turned tense.

No later revenue, funding round or valuation for Paradyes has been reported in the outlets we track, so the panel shows those as not publicly disclosed.

The pitch shows a founder choosing specific partners, one of them running a beauty company, over a better-sounding number from others.

shark_tank.pitch_summary: Paradyes pitched semi-permanent hair colours and asked ₹65 lakh for 1%. All the sharks bid, and the founders took Aman Gupta and Vineeta Singh's ₹65 lakh for 2%.

Yushika Jolly and Siddharth Raghuvanshi, based in Ahmedabad.

lessons: A bidding war gives founders leverage, but insisting on specific sharks can sour the room.
A shark with a company in the same category can be a strong partner, or a conflict; founders should weigh both.
Sharing real sales figures helps the sharks price the deal quickly.
